description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:243 (trait definition)

The trait surface ChatBackend has ~14 required + optional methods
plus the JmapBackend supertrait's get/changes/query family.
Implementing this trait correctly — particularly the contract
nuances flagged by the other findings in this epic — is a
substantial undertaking. A downstream consumer (kith, stoa, a
third-party) writes their own MemoryBackend equivalent and has
no way to verify they got the contract right without running
this crate's integration tests as a manual exercise.

Workspace AGENTS.md 'Defensive-code-forcing' relevant clause:
'API shapes that force every caller to write the same boilerplate
defensive check.' Generalised here to test boilerplate.

What's missing: a public test-harness module
(e.g. behind feature='test-harness') that exports a battery of
contract-compliance tests parameterised over any ChatBackend
implementation:

  #[cfg(feature = "test-harness")]
  pub mod test_harness {
      pub async fn run_contract_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);
      pub async fn run_space_set_atomicity_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);
      pub async fn run_invite_redemption_suite<B: ChatBackend>(backend: B);
      // ...
  }

Or a macro-based equivalent. The kit's own integration tests
become test_harness::run_*_suite(MemoryBackend::new()).await
calls; third-party backends opt in by adding the same calls in
their test suite.

This is a workspace-shape decision, not strictly required for
the kit to ship. Labeling 'opinion' because the engineering
basis is real (contract complexity, conformance gap) but the
fix is a multi-bead epic, not a single-bead edit.

Filing for visibility; the workspace may close as 'won't fix' or
escalate to its own epic depending on consumer demand.
title: API contract: ChatBackend trait has no test-shape macro / blanket harness for downstream backends
